How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-20 · vulnerability disclosure Palo Alto Networks
    Palo Alto Networks advisory: critical Java flaw affects on-premises Idira components

    According to a Palo Alto Networks security advisory dated 20 November 2026, a buffer overflow in the Java HotSpot JVM (CVE-2026-114938, rated critical by the vendor at CVSS-B 9.2) affects Idira Privilege Threat Analytics, the Idira Remote Access Connector and its CLI, and on-premises Idira Secure Access with an HTML5 Gateway, with fixed versions listed for each. The advisory says PAN-OS-based products are not affected, that SaaS products need no customer action, and that the company is not aware of malicious exploitation. It adds that review of the rest of the portfolio was continuing. Palo Alto Networks (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-18 · acquisition Palo Alto Networks
    Palo Alto Networks agrees to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at US$4.5 billion

    Palo Alto Networks announced on 18 November 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute, which provides a platform for post-training and running open-weight AI models. The company's release values the all-stock deal at US$4.5 billion, subject to adjustments, and expects it to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance. It does not name which existing product lines will change; the deal had not closed when this was recorded. The company said Protect AI's technology and team would become part of Prisma AIRS, and that Protect AI's chief executive Ian Swanson would join as vice president of product for Prisma AIRS.
